title: Heterogeneous ingest orchestrator for sequence-preserving log replay and correlation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an ingest orchestrator that preserves event sequence fidelity across heterogeneous sources (HTTP syslog, Fluentd, agent SDKs, cloud forwarders) while maintaining tenant isolation and correlation ID integrity. The goal is to provide a durable, order-aware ingestion path that supports: 1) deterministic replay for debugging/incident replay, 2) low-latency path for time-sensitive logs, and 3) graceful degradation to relaxed ordering for bulk nor critical telemetry. The component will sit in front of the existing ingestion mesh and emit canonical structured events to downstream storage (Loki and Elastic) with metadata for sequence and replay tokens. Key features: per-tenant session hashing and affinity, watermarking for late-arriving events, idempotent commit tokens for deduplication, local state for out-of-order buffering, and observability metrics for reorder-rate and replay success. This ticket covers design decisions, end-to-end implementation for the ingest proxy, and dashboards for latency/reorder monitoring.
tasks: Finalize design: session-affinity hash (tenant_id + stream_id) and partitioning model
Implement watermarking algorithm and late-arrival policy (hold window: configurable, default 2s)
Add idempotent commit token protocol for downstream storage writes
Extend ingest proxy to attach sequence_number and replay_token to canonical events
Build RocksDB-backed local buffer for short-term out-of-order hold and deduplication
Add backpressure signals to forwarders and a throttling policy for hot tenants
End-to-end test harness: high-throughput ordered append and deliberate reordering
Integration: Loki adapter with append-order TTL and Elastic adapter mapping for time-series queries
Create dashboards: ingestion-lag, reorder-rate, hold-window-drop-rate, dedup-rate, tenant-hotspots
Write runbook for operational recovery and replay using replay_tokens
comments: 2026-02-28: Maya Chen - Scoped initial problem statement after customer incident where multi-source joins broke due to reordering. Captured requirements and SLO targets (ingest-latency p99 <= 3s for hosted logs, reorder-rate < 0.05%).

2026-03-03: Arjun Patel - Spike results: per-tenant Kafka partitioning with session-hash gives stable ordering but increases partition count; measured 12% CPU overhead on proxy for watermarking and buffering under 10k qps per tenant. See spike notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Sequence+Ingest+Spike

2026-03-06: Design review - PM (Leah Ortiz) requested explicit fallback mode to relaxed-ordering for bulk telemetry and a metrics toggle. Design updated to include a policy flag and per-route priority labels.
2026-03-09: Security review requested - local RocksDB buffer will persist sequence metadata; product asked for encryption-at-rest and KMS integration. Security review ticket created and linked.

2026-03-11: Engineering sync - decided to implement idempotent commit tokens instead of global monotonic counters to avoid cross-region clock coordination. This simplifies replay and reduces coordination surface.
2026-03-12: PR created for ingest proxy changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/1234 (WIP). Initial unit tests for watermark edge cases added.
2026-03-14: Observability - added draft dashboard queries for reorder-rate and hold-window drops; linking Grafana dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest-sequence/sequence-monitoring
acceptance_criteria: Canonical events emitted with sequence_number and replay_token for all supported forwarders
End-to-end ordering preserved for per-session synthetic tests under 95th percentile load
Reorder-rate < 0.05% on canary tenants and alerting fires at 0.1%
Dashboards surface ingestion-lag and hold-window-drop-rate, runbook documented
Encryption of local buffer metadata verified by security review
notes: Trade-offs: preserving strict ordering adds buffering latency and increases state. We accept a small configurable hold window by default (2s) to balance latency vs. correctness; bulk telemetry routes will be able to opt-out to maximize throughput. Implementation will be staged: canary tenants -> dedicated tenant pool -> broader rollout. Consider future optimization: sequence compaction and shard migration tooling.
